purpose: Check whether five real actions can be compared correctly and measured consistently; this pilot is not a statistically conclusive paper result.
hypothesis: Action rankings may vary with prefix size, measured transfer capacity, and remaining generation; an action is allowed to be dominated everywhere in the sampled grid.

platform.precision: BF16 weights and KV; identical attention implementation and accumulation policy for all actions
platform.placement: Both physical hosts must verify the same canonical manifest and all model file hashes before allocation is considered ready.
platform.hardware_policy: Every action uses this same chosen platform; A6000 functional runs and original A800 performance results stay separate without rescaling.

start_gates: Do not run until main-model E0 passes on both A100 hosts for recompute, native fetch, holder execution, remote attention, and fixed progressive repair at BF16/TP1.

Match current E0: use one full-prefix prefill call for each P, followed by tokenwise suffix calls. A full concatenated prefix-plus-suffix forward is a separate numerical diagnostic, not this pilot's strict reference.

All five actions must produce finite logits within a documented E0-approved tolerance and exactly matching greedy token sequences for the paired pilot inputs; do not relax tolerance after seeing performance.
A common performance runner, real action implementations, request-level transport accounting, and application rate cap must exist and pass validation.
Both hosts must have sufficient verified local model storage and GPU memory; second-host staging and E0 completion are pending evidence, not assumed ready.

common_request_semantics.holder_background_load: None in this pilot; contention belongs to later experiments.
common_request_semantics.prefix_prefill: One forward call containing the complete P-token prefix, where P is 128 or 1024; identical prefix construction for every action and reference.
common_request_semantics.future_long_context: If longer contexts later require chunking, create a separate common chunk protocol for every action and recalibrate correctness and performance. This pilot introduces no chunking design.
common_request_semantics.suffix_execution: One token per forward call for every action and its reference.
common_request_semantics.generation: Greedy, fixed token count, EOS stopping disabled consistently; no sampling or speculative decoding.
common_request_semantics.reference: The same model revision, tokenizer, prompt tokens, position IDs, masks, cache layout, single full-prefix prefill, suffix tokenwise calls, and tokenwise decode shapes as the action under test.
common_request_semantics.prefix_preparation: For cache-hit actions, materialize the same prefix on the holder before the request barrier. For recompute, destination prefix reconstruction is inside the timed request. Destination starts without a reusable prefix for every action.
common_request_semantics.weights_and_engine: Both models and kernel paths are warm before every measured trial. All actions use one common engine, attention kernel policy, CPU staging policy, transport backend, rate limiter, and response destination.
common_request_semantics.request_inputs: All actions receive identical prefix/suffix token IDs and prefix identifiers. Input residency and request setup boundaries are fixed and documented.
common_request_semantics.paired_trials: Use the same deterministic input within each paired comparison. Reset per-request caches and action state before the barrier; retain only the explicitly allowed holder prefix.
common_request_semantics.barrier: A readiness barrier occurs before request acceptance. It may exclude common preparation only; action selection, per-request control/setup, serialization, queueing, and request-specific connection work remain inside request latency.
common_request_semantics.native_engine_control: Retain a separate native-HF tokenwise suffix/decode control with the identical full-prefix construction to quantify common custom-engine overhead; do not silently label the prototype optimized production serving.

actions.timed_work: Rebuild the complete P-token prefix in one timed prefill call, then run tokenwise suffix and generation at the destination.
Transfer and install the real prepared BF16 prefix KV, then run suffix and generation at the destination; include sender staging, copies, and setup.
Send the actual request to the existing holder, execute suffix and generation there, and deliver each generated token to the common response destination.
Run genuine remote attention against holder-resident prefix KV, with real activation/result transfer and destination continuation.
Execute a fixed, documented E0-validated repair schedule with real cache migration and continuation; log progress and any duplicated work.
actions.schedule_status: Must be frozen before pilot measurements; no schedule tuning on measured trial outcomes.

grid.rate_cap_scope: Apply the same per-direction cap to all inter-host request data/control traffic for every action; report the achieved rate. These values are proposed application caps, not measured physical-link speeds.
grid.rtt: No added delay in this pilot; record measured baseline RTT separately.
grid.ordering: Record a fixed random seed and randomize action order within paired repetitions to reduce order effects.
grid.interpretation: The grid and repetition counts test feasibility and coarse action ordering only. Preserve raw trials; report medians/ranges descriptively without significance or tail guarantees.

measurement.main_timer: Use one destination monotonic clock. Record t_accept before action-specific work, t_first_token, t_final_token, and t_settled after required completion acknowledgement and background drain. Token-completion and settled latencies are distinct; never subtract clocks from different hosts.
measurement.ttft: Request acceptance to delivery of the first generated token, including suffix processing and all request-specific setup and queueing.
measurement.itl_and_tbt: Inter-token latency/time-between-tokens use the same consecutive token-delivery timestamp differences. Retain the raw sequence; do not count these aliases as independent metrics.
measurement.completion_latency: Request acceptance to final token delivery; additionally report time until any request-owned background repair/transfer finishes if it outlives token generation.
measurement.tail_reporting: No p95/p99 claim from three repetitions or a five-repeat shortcut. Formal request-level tails require the later E7 workload, enough independent request samples, recorded sample counts, and an explicit estimation protocol.
measurement.bytes: Required: transmitted tensor payload bytes and application frame bytes (length/header/payload) accepted by socket sends, per direction and request, reconciled against peer receive counts. Optional: separately validated physical-wire capture with its layer/scope stated. Application counts do not include TCP/IP headers, retransmissions, or Ethernet framing.
measurement.wire_accounting_gate: Lack of validated physical-wire capture must be marked physical_wire_bytes=null and wire_measurement_available=false. It does not block this action-latency pilot, whose bandwidth treatment is an explicitly named application socket-byte cap; it forbids physical network bandwidth-savings or NIC-traffic claims.
measurement.cpu_and_queues: End-to-end latency includes sender CPU serialization/staging, receiver handling, queue waits, rate-limiter waits, GPU copies, synchronization, and response delivery. Report their breakdown only using a separate instrumented run when needed.
performance_path_exclusions: No full-vocabulary diagnostic logits are transferred in main performance trials.
No cache hashing or reference recomputation is performed inside the main performance interval.
No CUDA per-operation timing events, NVTX ranges, profiler capture, or diagnostic per-operation synchronization is enabled in the main performance run.
measurement.separate_diagnostics: Run correctness/logit comparisons and CUDA-event/NVTX profiling separately with matching configurations. A full concatenated prefix-plus-suffix forward may be retained as a separate numerical diagnostic; it does not replace the common full-prefix-then-tokenwise-suffix reference. Preserve links to their trial/configuration IDs, and do not combine diagnostic timing with performance samples.
measurement.settled_latency: t_settled - t_accept; includes final completion acknowledgement and request-owned background drain.
measurement.post_token_drain_latency: t_settled - t_final_token; report separately instead of adding it silently to response completion.

required_components_not_asserted_ready: Main-model, same-shape BF16 E0 evidence for all five actions on both hosts.
Unified request runner with common warm-state preparation, deterministic paired inputs, and actual response delivery timestamps.
An implemented and fixed progressive repair schedule plus verified remote attention.
A shared application rate limiter with measured achieved throughput and complete request traffic coverage.
Separate correctness, profiling, and minimally instrumented performance modes.
Verified request-level tensor payload and application-frame accounting, reconciled sends/receives, setup/queue completion tracking, and an explicit null marker for any unmeasured physical wire bytes.
stop_and_reporting_rules: Stop on model/revision/hash mismatch, failed E0, invalid numeric output, greedy mismatch, missing real action, OOM, or differing prefix/suffix call shapes.
Stop and repair the harness if diagnostic traffic enters the performance path or action-specific work falls outside the defined timer.
Preserve failures and dominated actions. Do not remove unfavorable cells, silently change caps, or manufacture a region where an action wins.
Report ties and unstable orderings as unresolved; three repetitions cannot establish a robust crossover.
Any revised grid or execution schedule creates a new protocol version, with reasons recorded before rerunning.

resources_and_completion.allocation: Two A100 80GB GPUs on two physical hosts; actual CPU/RAM/time requests follow measured main-model E0 and first pilot timings.
resources_and_completion.gpu_hour_budget: Not yet estimated. After an instrumented feasibility run, estimate allocated GPU-hours as two times allocation wall-hours, including initialization, preparation, warmups, barriers, retries, and measured trials; update from scheduler accounting.
resources_and_completion.completion: All eight cells retain three valid paired measurements for all five real actions, correct separation of diagnostics, validated application-frame traffic accounting, and documented failures/uncertainty. Record separately whether physical-wire capture exists. Completion establishes prototype feasibility only; formal performance and tail claims remain downstream.

revision_reason: Before any E1 run: disambiguate final-token vs settled latency; make application-frame byte accounting the required transport metric and report physical wire bytes only when separately validated.
